articles.title: Nya tullar, volatila börser och stark makrodata i USA
articles.heading: Morning Alert
articles.fulltext:
Internationellt
Börserna föll igen under gårdagen men framför allt i USA så vände det något på slutet vilket resulterade i tämligen små fall i förhållande till när det var som värst under dagen. S&P 500 föll 0,3% och tekniktunga Nasdaq med 0,6% men var som mest ner runt 4,6% under dagen. Det är främst AI-oron som fortsätter tynga börserna men att Trump återigen vädrade tankar om nya tullar (mer nedan) hjälpte heller inte till. Helt klart är i alla fall att osäkerheten och därmed volatiliteten är stor just nu men notera också att handeln i USA är stängd idag pga. Thanksgiving. 
Trots den starka makrodatan under dagen (se nedan) så fortsatte amerikanska räntor att tappa och ökat intresse för säkrare statspapperen när börsen skakar verkar som en rimlig drivkraft. US-dollarn tappade också generellt något under gårdagen. Oljepriset tog ett kliv högre för fösta gången på flera dagar men på 95 dollar per fat är nivåerna fortsatt betydligt lägre än i början av november. Asien har tagit rygg på återhämtningen som skedde i slutet av börsdagen i USA och indexen är generellt upp med AI-tunga Taiwan-indexet i toppen på +2,8%. Även börsterminerna indikerar en positiv start i USA men än mer i Europa idag. 
Tullar på tapeten igen. 
Igår tillkännagav Trump en rad nya tullar mot 14 länder däribland EU, Kina, Japan och Sydkorea medan Norge klarade sig utan. Tullar på upp till 20% föreslås för specifika varugrupper där Kina och Vietnam föreslås få de högsta nivåerna medan EU förslås en nivå på 15%. De här tullarna kommer inte implementeras omedelbart utan det antyds att det kommer dröja månader innan de kan träda i kraft. 
Högre inflation och tillväxt i USA.
 Feds favoritmått på inflationen kärn-PCE överraskade igår något på uppsidan mätt i årstakt när den kom in på 3,3% mot förväntade 3,2% att jämföras med 3,1% i september. Samtidigt överraskade den andra mätningen av BNP för tredje kvartalet också på uppsidan med en kraftig uppgång om 4,3% snarare än den förväntade om 3,5% (uppräknad årstakt). Tillväxten har fortsatt främst drivits av stark konsumtion, men också av en ökning av för IT-utrustning och programvara vilket vi betraktar som ett mått på AI-investeringar. Det finns därför fog för viss oro framöver om AI-frossan håller i sig och båda dessa tillväxtdrivande komponenter får sig lite av en törn. Den lite högre inflationssiffran tillsammans med starkare tillväxt stärker caset för att Fed höjer räntan i december och att de signalerar en eller fler höjningar i deras prognoser för 2027. Notera att vi igår, redan innan datan, la till en höjning i mars till våra prognoser – mer 
här
. 
Dagens agenda är relativt tunn
 där USA är stängt för Thanksgiving. Vi har att se fram emot tyskt konsumentförtroende, norsk BNP för tredje kvartalet, Riksgäldens rapport om upplåningen (mer nedan), ett tal från Riksbankens Jansson (Svensk penningpolitik i en osäker omvärld) och så börjar ett två dagars Euro summit idag. 
Norsk BNP för tredje kvartalet idag och budget igår.
 BNP i fastlandsekonomien ökade med 0,3% under andra kvartalet, medan tillväxten under första kvartalet reviderades marginellt nedåt. Det tyder på lägre årlig tillväxt i år än vad som tidigare förväntades. Vi, konsensus och Norges Bank är dock eniga om att även tredje kvartalet kommer att visa en ökning på 0,3% där data från produktionssidan i stort sett är neutrala medan det är mer blandat på efterfrågesidan. Efter intensiva förhandlingar presenterades ett reviderat statsbudgetförslag för 2027 igår men då Miljöpartier valde att stå utanför uppgörelsen är det inte säkert att budgeten kommer få majoritetsstöd i parlamentet.  
Sverige
Riksgälden rapporterar om upplåning idag kl. 09:30.
 Vi tror att Riksgälden minskar utbudet av nominella obligationsemissioner något under 2027 jämfört med planerna från maj och att antalet veckovisa auktioner minskar från 48 till 45, vilket innebär en total på 225 miljarder under 2027. De kommer att invänta en formell begäran från Riksbanken innan man inkluderar en ökad emission av valutaobligationer i prognosen, men kommer sannolikt redan nu att diskutera möjliga konsekvenser i rapporten. Läs mer i 
360 Sweden
. 
Svenska producentpriser steg i oktober.
 Producentprisindex, som publicerades för oktober igår, steg med 0,9%. Det var något överraskande då vi snarare trott på en nedgång om 0,2%. Uppgången kom dels då elpriserna fortsatt upp istället för att som vi tänkt tillfälligt sjunka. Därtill steg priserna på exportvaror och konsumtionsvaror något och vi ser även att ett visst uppåttrycket från växelkursen troligen också bidrog. Angående elpriserna noterar vi återigen kraftiga uppgångar inför helgen och november som helhet kommer stark bidra uppåt på kommande PPI.

articles.title: Snap election in Spain – a solution to the parliamentary deadlock?
articles.heading: Euro area outlook
articles.fulltext:
Spain will hold a snap election on 29 November following a prolonged period of parliamentary deadlock. Opinion polls point to a change of government. The next government will inherit a relatively favourable economic backdrop, with strong growth and a declining public debt-to-GDP ratio. The main risk is continued political uncertainty and difficulties in passing budgets and reforms, rather than an immediate deterioration in public finances.
Key points
Snap election to break parliamentary deadlock
Strong economy provides a favourable starting point
A stable and reform-oriented Spanish government could help contain risk premia
Snap election following parliamentary deadlock
In early October, Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez called a snap election for 29 November after the government’s proposals to address the housing crisis were voted down. The proposals included stronger protection against evictions and extensions of expiring rental contracts. The housing crisis has triggered widespread protests across Spain. However, the underlying reason for calling the election was the parliamentary deadlock. Sánchez’s government – comprising the Socialist Party (PSOE) and the left-wing alliance Sumar, which has been reconstituted as Frente Amplio ahead of the election – lacks a stable parliamentary majority. The government has relied on support from smaller regional parties, including Catalan separatists and Basque nationalists. The fragmented parliament has made it particularly difficult to pass new budgets. Spain has not adopted a new budget since 2023. The aim of the snap election is therefore to secure stronger parliamentary support. The next scheduled general election was due to take place in 2027.
A shift to the right?
Opinion polls show a relatively tight race between the two largest parties, the conservative Partido Popular (PP) and the centre-left social democratic party PSOE, with PP holding a slight lead. Together with the national-conservative Vox, however, PP appears to be in a position to secure a parliamentary majority, provided the two parties can reach an agreement on governing together.
PP leader Alberto Núñez Feijóo is currently seen as the favourite to become Spain’s next prime minister. However, Sánchez has a track record of strong electoral performances despite political headwinds, and the possibility of him remaining in office cannot be ruled out. Increased fragmentation among smaller left-wing parties could, however, make it particularly difficult for Sánchez to secure sufficient parliamentary support to govern. A defeat for PSOE would mark a historic turning point, given that the party has governed Spain for almost 30 years across three separate periods since the restoration of democracy following the death of dictator Francisco Franco in 1975.
The election campaign has been dominated by the housing crisis, corruption scandals surrounding PSOE, the handling of migrants in the Spanish enclave of Ceuta, and high but varying levels of regional debt and borrowing requirements. Railway safety has also come into focus following two major train accidents that claimed more than 100 lives. A victory for the right would mark the end of eight years of Sánchez and socialist-led governments.
Strong economy provides a tailwind for the next government
Spain has enjoyed strong growth since the post-pandemic recovery. Several factors explain this performance: a robust services sector supported by tourism, immigration, increased investment financed by the EU’s recovery fund, and a more favourable energy mix that has enabled Spain to weather recent energy crises better than countries such as Germany. The next government will thus inherit a relatively favourable economic starting point, with a high but declining public debt-to-GDP ratio.
Implications for fiscal policy
The fragmented parliament has meant that Spain has not adopted a new budget since 2023. A functioning PP-led majority government, supported by Vox, could reduce uncertainty and facilitate the budget process, while a persistently fragmented parliament risks delaying reforms and budget decisions. Public debt stood at just over 100% of GDP in 2025 but is expected by the European Commission to fall below this level this year. Meanwhile, the budget deficit is projected to widen slightly to just over 2.5% of GDP in 2026 before narrowing to 2.2% in 2027.
France’s strained fiscal position has drawn attention to other highly indebted countries, including Spain. Spanish sovereign bond spreads over Germany have also widened somewhat, but considerably less than their French counterparts. In our view, developments in France and broader risks surrounding European public finances are more important drivers of Spanish government bonds than the election outcome itself. However, a stable and reform-oriented Spanish government could help contain risk premia.
PP’s election manifesto includes tax cuts, a more restrictive immigration policy and a less ambitious climate policy. A stable PP-led government could reduce political uncertainty, facilitate reforms and improve the prospects for continued fiscal consolidation. However, the scope for consolidation will depend on the specific policy measures implemented. Proposed tax cuts and higher defence spending, for example, could make it more difficult to reduce the budget deficit.
The risks associated with the snap election primarily concern the ability to form a government capable of making decisions and implementing its policies. Strong economic growth should facilitate fiscal consolidation. However, successful consolidation requires a government with sufficient parliamentary support to pass new budgets. Rolling over previous budgets is not a sustainable long-term solution if Spain is to reduce its high level of public debt.

articles.title: Large SEK selling need in November
articles.heading: Rebalancing flows
articles.fulltext:
Our model estimates that typical Swedish portfolio managers have relatively large SEK selling requirements in their monthly currency rebalancing this November. The most pronounced flow is USD buying vs SEK selling. The stylised portfolio lost 1.1% in November, bringing its year-to-date return down to 3.4%.
SEK selling requirements
This November, rebalancing implies a historically relatively large SEK selling need of -0.6% of the portfolio and a USD buying need of 0.5% of the portfolio.
Large need to buy USD/SEK in November
Historical outcomes of SEK rebalancing needs
Source: SEB
Portfolio implications 
Currency hedge:
The stylised portfolio used in our analysis lost 1.1% in November, which implies only a small need to rebalance the hedge ratios (corresponding to -0.1% of the portfolio).
Bonds & Equity: 
Relative monthly performance points to a small need to buy Swedish equities (corresponding to 0.04% of the portfolio) and a need to sell Swedish bonds (corresponding to -0.52% of the portfolio). Together, the allocation rebalancing implies net SEK selling of -0.48% of the portfolio.
Market developments November
All in all:
 Combining the hedge and allocation rebalancing needs results in total SEK selling of -0.58% of the portfolio in November.

articles.title: Continued rate hikes amid a tug-of-war between inflation and AI equity concerns
articles.heading: Fed policy outlook
articles.fulltext:
Hawkish comments from several Fed officials suggest that the Fed will raise rates again in December and that policymakers will project at least one further hike in 2027. We now expect the Fed to hike twice more, in December this year and in March next year, although developments in the Middle East, inflation, AI and financial markets will be key. Fed Chair Warsh has embarked on a reform agenda at the Fed, but at least as far as communication policy is concerned, he does not appear to have the rest of the Fed on board.
Key points
Fed to raise rates and rate projections in December
We revise our Fed forecast to include another hike in March
Fed officials push back against Warsh’s communication strategy
After raising its policy rate in September – for the first time in just over three years – the US Federal Reserve left rates unchanged at 3.75–4.00% at its 27–28 October meeting. According to the minutes of the October meeting, however, almost all participants expected further monetary tightening in the months ahead, broadly in line with the projections presented at the September meeting. In September, a majority of Fed participants (10 out of 18) signalled that one additional hike in 2026 would be sufficient, but almost as many (eight participants) expected the Fed to raise rates at least once more in 2027. Fed Chair Kevin Warsh wants Fed officials to stop publishing projections and once again refrained from submitting his own projections.
High CPI inflation could prompt Waller to vote for a 50bp hike
Since the October meeting, data have pointed to a continued surprisingly resilient economy. Employment growth was stronger than expected in October, household demand remained robust and inflationary pressures were unexpectedly strong and fairly broad-based, according to the October CPI report. Meanwhile, signals from Fed officials have become increasingly hawkish. Some officials, most notably Christopher Waller, have even begun discussing a 50bp hike in December, a view shared by at least one other participant, according to the October minutes. The majority, however, appear to favour a more cautious approach, with smaller but more frequent rate hikes, either at every meeting or every other meeting. Most Fed officials have said that rates need to rise further, and some, though not all, have referred to rate hikes in the plural. New York Fed President and FOMC Vice Chair John Williams recently said that he supported further tightening but saw no need for “dramatic” action, a clear signal that he does not favour 50bp hikes. He does not, however, exclude moving at consecutive meetings, if needed. Fed Vice Chair Philip Jefferson has also struck a more balanced tone in his speeches.
Fed divided over the rationale for raising rates
We still see the Fed as divided between those who see an immediate need for tightening to prevent inflation from accelerating further and those who view rate hikes as a precautionary measure but do not actually wish to restrain growth. The further acceleration in inflation following the rise in energy prices is a concern for Fed officials, given the risk that more than five years of above-target inflation could start to affect both corporate pricing behaviour and wage-setting. Fed officials have also begun placing greater emphasis on the inflationary risks associated with the AI build-out, which, at least initially, is seen as an upside risk to both growth and inflation. However, most participants, at least in October, viewed the inflationary pressures stemming from tariffs, energy prices and the AI build-out as temporary and expected inflation to return to target over time. Market-implied inflation expectations have declined, driven by falling fuel prices, while household inflation expectations have remained stable. Lower energy prices do not appear to have affected the tone of Fed communication but should help alleviate concerns, provided energy prices continue to decline in line with futures prices.
Equity market turmoil tightens financial conditions
Another reason to proceed cautiously is the recent equity market turmoil. Like many other observers, the Fed believes that rising equity prices have helped sustain household consumption. In October, participants assessed financial conditions as supportive, partly reflecting elevated equity valuations. If AI stocks continue to fall, putting further downward pressure on broader equity markets, the Fed may no longer regard financial conditions as equally supportive. At the same time, the Fed’s own rate hikes appear to have contributed to equity market jitters. The decline in AI stocks can partly be attributed to a less favourable political landscape in the US, with pledges from Democrats at state level to slow the pace of the AI build-out and (likely empty) threats from President Trump to impose punitive taxes on companies building data centres abroad. However, we also believe that the decline reflects the renewed rise in long-term interest rates, which both increases borrowing costs for AI companies and raises the discount rate applied to their earnings. During November, the 10-year US Treasury yield has occasionally traded above 5% again and, as before, the increase has been driven by rising real yields rather than higher break-even inflation rates.
The unexpectedly high October CPI reading and Waller’s comments about 50bp hikes prompted rates markets to raise their expectations of Fed tightening, at one point pricing in more than three additional hikes. Following the equity market decline, expectations were scaled back again. At the time of writing, rates markets are pricing in just over 2½ hikes by next summer.
Fed to raise rates and rate projections in December
At the December meeting, Fed officials will both decide on the policy rate and present updated projections for the economy and interest rates. We expect the Fed to raise rates to 4.00–4.25%, with unanimous support for further tightening (although we cannot rule out Waller and possibly another member voting in favour of a 50bp hike). At the same time, we expect the median rate projection to shift towards one additional hike next year.
We revise our Fed forecast to include another hike in March
For some time, we have forecasted a Fed rate hike in December, followed by unchanged rates. However, the higher-than-expected October CPI reading, combined with hawkish Fed comments and persistent upside risks to inflation, now leads us to expect another hike in March next year. Persistently elevated energy prices have increased the risk of spillover effects on other prices, for example through higher transport costs. Indicators such as producer prices for consumer goods and services point to continued upward pressure on consumer price inflation in the near term, and we have revised our core inflation forecasts for both this year and next year slightly higher. Lower oil prices over the past month have somewhat reduced the risk of indirect effects, however.
Our revised forecast implies that the policy rate will peak at 4.25–4.50%. This is above Fed officials’ estimates of the longer-run neutral rate. Estimates of the neutral rate vary considerably among Fed officials, but all September projections fell within a range of 2.9–3.9%, with a median of 3.2%. We expect the Fed to cut rates towards the end of 2027 and three more times in 2028, bringing the policy rate to 3.25–3.50% by the end of 2028. The endpoint is unchanged from our previous forecast.
Risks on both the upside and downside
Developments in the Middle East conflict and their impact on energy prices, inflation data over the coming months, the strength of the AI build-out and developments in financial markets will all be key to assessing the monetary policy outlook. We see risks to our forecast in both directions.
The Fed’s preferred inflation measure, core PCE, has been above core CPI since late last year, contrary to the historical pattern. We expect the two measures to converge again, with core PCE inflation peaking slightly above 3% at the end of this year before gradually approaching the 2% target again by the end of 2028.
As regards the war with Iran, President Trump continues to send mixed signals about renewed attacks. Meanwhile, the blockade of Iran has put the country in a difficult position, prompting Iran to attack US targets in the region in an attempt to pressure the US into accepting Iran’s terms for ending the war. Should hostilities intensify, the risk of an even more prolonged period of elevated energy prices would increase, adding further upward pressure on US inflation. Continued equity market turmoil, on the other hand, could prompt the Fed to proceed more cautiously, partly to avoid exacerbating the situation at a time when deteriorating financing conditions for AI companies could threaten growth, both directly through a smaller contribution from the AI build-out and indirectly through negative wealth effects on consumption.
Fed officials push back against Warsh’s communication strategy
Fed Chair Warsh has established five task forces tasked with improving the Fed’s monetary policy analysis and practices in the areas of communication, balance sheet policy, economic data, productivity and labour markets, and inflation. The intention was for the task forces to complete their work towards the end of the year. We may therefore gain some new insights from Warsh at the December press conference. One issue that has come into focus is the Fed’s communication policy, with Warsh seeking both to abandon forward guidance on upcoming policy decisions and to stop publishing individual economic and interest rate projections.
Recent communication from other Fed officials suggests that Warsh has struggled to bring his colleagues on board. While Warsh has been cautious about elaborating on his views regarding the future path of interest rates, comments and speeches from other Fed officials have, if anything, become more frequent. Several officials also appear to argue that the less the Fed says about interest rates, the faster and more aggressively it may be forced to tighten, as it would no longer be able to rely on financial markets to do some of the work for it. Several officials have also explicitly stated that they see benefits in continuing to publish individual projections. It will therefore be interesting to hear what Warsh has to say on this issue in December, as well as whether he intends to maintain the practice of holding a press conference after every meeting in the years ahead.

articles.title: Tech optimism falters again
articles.heading: Nordic Alert
articles.fulltext:
Global key stories
Despite 
presidential support and standing ovations
, Jensen Huang's return to Nvidia still does not cure the market's underlying concerns about AI valuations and future profitability. Stock markets in both Europe and the US fell yesterday after Monday's AI-led rally lost momentum, with Nvidia down just over 6 percent following Monday's sharp gain. The Nasdaq fell 1.5 percent while the Dow Jones went against the trend and rose 0.9 percent – possibly a sign of rotation from AI companies to the broader industrial sector. Yields fell slightly and the dollar weakened after recently reaching a 20-month high against the euro. Stock market declines continue in Asia today, and futures indicate a negative opening in the US. Europe, however, appears to be heading towards a cautiously positive opening.
Markets now turn to today's US PCE inflation and growth figures. 
French consumer confidence and details on German Q3 GDP are also on the agenda, as are Swedish producer prices. Australian inflation figures came in surprisingly hot this morning but failed to support the AUD.
US inflation is expected to rise.
 US PCE inflation for October is the last inflation figure before the Fed's rate decision on December 9. We anticipate that core PCE, Fed's preferred inflation measure, will rise 0.3 percent month-on-month for the third consecutive month, lifting the year-on-year rate from 3.1 to 3.3 percent. The Fed thus receives another important piece of the puzzle ahead of the December meeting at a time when both growth and inflation signals have been stronger than expected.
We 
change our Fed forecast following hawkish comments from FOMC-members and now expect two further hikes: one in December and one in March next year
. We previously forecasted only one hike in December – more on this 
here
 (in Swedish).
AI-driven growth. 
We also receive 
the second estimate of US GDP for the third quarter. The initial estimate showed growth of 3.4 percent year-on-year, with both investments and household consumption contributing strongly; AI-related investments are a very important driver of growth. Income, spending, private consumption and new durable goods orders etc. are published as well, and the Fed releases its Beige Book in the evening.
Plenty to read in Ögat:
 We update our Fed forecast and write about the tug-of-war between AI and inflation concerns, comment on the situation ahead of Sunday's snap elections in Spain, analyze the data center boom as an important driver for the Nordic industry and review the seasonal pattern of the krona. We also write about the price spreads between crude oil and distillates such as gasoline and diesel, and about the outlook for electricity prices ahead of winter. Texts are in Swedish and you find them 
here.
Nordic key stories
Swedish producer prices.
 We expect PPI to fall by 0.2 percent compared to September, mainly due to temporarily lower electricity prices. At the same time, a slightly weaker krona is expected to put some upward pressure on producer prices for consumer goods. Despite higher energy prices, we assess that there are still few signs of broader indirect effects via international producer prices.
Parliament will vote on Ulf Kristersson (M) as prime minister for a government consisting of M, C, KD, and L
 on Monday. Speaker Andreas Norlén said yesterday that Kristersson has been careful to point out that he did not know how the Centre Party would position. However, 
SVT reports
 that according to unnamed sources,
 the Centre Party's Thand Ringqvist had pointed out two possible ways forward during a meeting on Tuesday evening: either join a centre-right government or head towards a snap election. Voters seem to have tired of the lengthy negotiations; a 
new opinion poll
 clearly shows lower support for both the Centre Party and the Social Democrats.

articles.title: Nya börsfall
articles.heading: Morning Alert
articles.fulltext:
Internationellt
Trots 
presidentstöd och stående ovationer
 botar Jensen Huangs återkomst i Nvidia ändå inte marknadens underliggande oro för AI-bolagens värderingar och framtida lönsamhet. Börserna i både Europa och USA backade under gårdagen efter att måndagens AI-ledda uppgång tappat fart, med Nvidia ned drygt 6 procent efter måndagens kraftiga uppgång. Nasdaq föll 1,5 procent medan Dow Jones gick mot strömmen och steg 0,9 procent – möjligen ett tecken på rotation från rena AI-bolag till den bredare industrisektorn. Samtidigt sjönk långräntor något och dollarn försvagades efter att nyligen ha nått sin högsta nivå på 20 månader mot euron. Börsnedgångarna fortsätter i Asien idag och börsterminer tyder på negativ öppning i USA. Europa ser dock ut att öppna försiktigt positivt.
Marknadens fokus riktas nu mot dagens amerikanska PCE-inflation och tillväxtsiffror. 
Franskt konsumentförtroende och detaljer kring tysk BNP för tredje kvartalet står också på agendan, liksom svenska producentpriser.
Amerikansk inflation väntas stiga.
 En av veckans viktigaste hållpunkter är amerikansk PCE-inflation för oktober, den sista inflationssiffran före Feds räntebesked den 9 december. Prognosen är att kärn-PCE, som är Feds föredragna inflationsmått, stiger 0,3 procent i månadstakt för tredje månaden i rad, vilket också skulle innebära att årstakten tickar upp med två tiondelar till 3,3 procent. Fed får därmed ytterligare en viktig pusselbit inför decembermötet i ett läge där både tillväxt- och inflationssignalerna varit starkare än väntat. 
Vi 
ändrar vår Fed-prognos i spåren av hökaktiga kommentarer och förväntar oss nu två ytterligare höjningar: en i december och en i mars nästa år
. Tidigare trodde vi att Fed skulle nöja sig med en höjning i december – mer om detta 
här
.
AI-driven tillväxt. 
Inflationen publiceras samtidigt som den andra beräkningen av amerikansk BNP för tredje kvartalet. Den första uppskattningen visade en tillväxt på 3,4 procent i uppräknad årstakt, där både investeringar och hushållskonsumtion bidrog starkt. AI-relaterade investeringar är en mycket viktig drivkraft bakom tillväxten i USA. Utöver inflation och BNP publiceras även statistik över bland annat inkomster, konsumtion och orderingången för varaktiga varor, och under kvällen släpper Fed sin Beige Book.
Fullmatad Ögat:
 Vi uppdaterar vår Fed-prognos och skriver om dragkampen mellan AI- och inflations-oro, kommenterar läget inför söndagens nyval i Spanien, analyserar datacenterboomen som en viktig drivkraft för nordisk industri och går igenom säsongsmönstret för kronans utveckling. Vi skriver också om prisskillnaden mellan råolja och destillat som bensin och diesel och om utsikterna för elpriserna inför vintern. Ögat hittar du 
här
!
Sverige
Svenska producentpriser.
 På hemmaplan publiceras producentprisindex för oktober. Vi räknar med att PPI sjunker 0,2 procent jämfört med föregående månad, främst till följd av tillfälligt lägre elpriser. Samtidigt väntas en något svagare krona ge ett visst uppåttryck på producentpriserna för konsumentvaror. Trots högre energipriser bedömer vi att det fortfarande finns få tecken på bredare indirekta effekter via internationella producentpriser.
Ulf Kristersson (M) prövas som statsminister för en regering bestående av M, C, KD och L
 på måndag. Talman Andreas Norlén sa under gårdagen att Kristersson varit noga med att påpeka att han inte visste hur Centerpartiet skulle ställa sig. Enligt 
uppgifter till SVT
ska dock Centerpartiets Thand Ringqvist ha pekat ut två möjliga vägar framåt i regeringsbyggandet under tisdagskvällens stormöte: antingen ingå i en Alliansregering eller gå mot ett extraval. Väljarna tycks ha tröttnat på de segdragna förhandlingarna; en 
ny opinionsundersökning
 visar tydligt lägre stöd för både Centerpartiet och Socialdemokraterna.

articles.title: Ovanligt svängigt säsongsmönster för kronan
articles.heading: Ögat
articles.fulltext:
Kronan har en tendens att stärkas i december. Under de senaste 15 åren har kronan stärkts mot euron och norska kronen 12 av åren, och mot dollarn i 11 av åren. Tidigare fanns även ett mönster där kronan försvagades i början av månaden och främst för att pensionsbolagen brukar köpa stora mängder utländska aktier i början av månaden. Denna säsongseffekt har dock klingat av de senaste åren.
Nyval i Spanien
– lösningen på den parlamentariska låsningen?
Spanien går till nyval den 29 november efter en längre tid med parlamentariska låsningar. Opinionsmätningarna pekar mot ett regeringsskifte.
Inte bara olja – stor skillnad i pris mellan produkter 
Kriget i Persiska viken har lyft oljepriset. Prisskillnader mellan råolja och olika destillat som diesel och bensin har också ökat markant. Sammanfattningsvis drar en mängd olika faktorer i olika riktning.
Tuff vinter med höga elpriser
Risker på uppsidan för olje- och energipriser kopplade till Irankriget har under hösten materialiserats och nu även spridits till elpriserna. Kommande vinter i Europa och Sverige ser därför ut att bli dyr.
Fed fortsätter höja i en dragkamp mellan inflations- och AI-oro 
Hökaktiga Fed-kommentarer pekar mot att Fed höjer igen i december och att ledamöterna spår åtminstone en ytterligare höjning under 2027. Vi räknar nu med att Fed höjer två gånger till.
Datacenterboomen – viktig drivkraft för nordisk industri
Den globala investeringsvågen inom artificiell intelligens och datacenter är en viktig förklaring till den starka vinstutvecklingen i nordisk industri. Sid 11. FX Sales: USD/SEK handlar starkt – läge att säkra? Marknadsförväntningar om fler räntehöjningar från Federal Reserve har, tillsammans med en nervositet för höga AI-värderingar, stärkt dollarn, vilket skapar ett bra tillfälle att låsa in USD/SEK.

articles.title: COP 31 ends in deep divisions
articles.heading: Sustainable Finance Outlook Brief
articles.fulltext: COP31 ended in deep divisions over fossil fuels and climate finance, without an overarching agreement. Despite stronger national climate plans, current pledges remain insufficient to avoid overshooting 1.5°C. The summit highlighted electrification’s emissions-reduction potential and AI’s growing environmental footprint. COP31’s breakdown is unlikely to alter EU climate policy, while US re-entry into the UNFCCC remains unlikely before 2029. Mobilising more climate finance, including private capital from developed markets, could help ease negotiating deadlock.

articles.title: Major stock market rallies, do they continue today?
articles.heading: Nordic Alert
articles.fulltext:
Global key stories
Jensen Huang is being brought back.
 At least by Nvidia’s board,
 following pressure from President Trump.
 According to Bloomberg,
 the decision was made at breakneck speed,
 without consulting any parts of the executive leadership other than the board.
 Huang is now returning after 10 days,
 prompting news agencies to dust off the old "too big to fail" concept—though this time applied to a CEO.
 Government sources say the move was made in the best interest of shareholders,
 employees,
 partners,
 and customers.
 The news sent Nvidia’s stock rebounding by 31% (!
),
 after having lost 50% since October 6,
 though it remains down a net 31% from its peak.
After a couple of turbulent weeks,
 the event caused global stock markets to completely reverse direction.
 The S&P 500 rose 4.
7%,
 the Nasdaq 6.
5%,
 and Sweden’s OMXSPI 2.
5%.
 The momentum is rippling through the trading system,
 with Japan’s Nikkei up 4% this morning and the tech-heavy Korean KOSPI up 7%.
 Stock futures are pointing toward slight gains today.
 Ten-year government bond yields have edged down slightly,
 while two-year yields are largely unchanged or up just a basis point or two.
 The US dollar strengthened and is now trading at 1.
09,
 a level not seen since the most turbulent days around "Liberation Day.
" Crude oil prices have also worked their way down below USD 90 per barrel,
 the lowest level since late August.
Today’s economic calendar partially picks up where yesterday’s PMIs left off,
 with further survey data on future confidence.
 In Germany,
 the major Ifo survey is due out,
 alongside consumer confidence in the US.
 Yesterday’s PMI surveys painted a mixed picture across Europe,
 with continued weakness in France offset by both the manufacturing and service sectors in Germany taking an increasingly positive view of the near future.
Nordic key stories
In
Sweden 360
 (biweekly),
 the
 financial focus 
is on expectations of a lower supply of nominal bonds when the Swedish National Debt Office  (SNDO) releases its new borrowing report on Thursday.
 Regarding the SEK,
 it is simply noted that recent stock market jitters are weighing heavily on the currency.
 We are also kicking off this year’s review of the krona’s December performance.
 Historically,
PPM flows
 have weakened the SEK,
 though this pattern has been less clear in recent years.
 On the contrary,
 the krona has tended to strengthen ahead of these flows.
Today's 
political focus 
is on the Speaker’s rounds of talks (starting at 9:
30 AM) ahead of a potential third prime ministerial vote.
 The outcome is as hard to predict as the sense is strong that the climate of cooperation on the red-green side has taken a hit in recent days.
 The Centre Party is now also announcing that the uncertainty has prompted them to leave the door slightly ajar to what current prime minister Kristersson has to offer.
 This morning,
 SvD/Demoskop presented a new opinion poll (paywalled link here) in which the Moderate Party (M) reaches its highest level in over ten years.
 This aligns with other recent polls; public opinion regarding the weeks following the election has primarily benefited M.
 The Liberals (L) are below the 4% parliamentary threshold,
 and both the Christian Democrats (KD) and the Sweden Democrats (SD) are polling lower than in the general election.
 The Social Democrats (S) are losing support in this survey,
 though not as sharply as in the latest Novus poll,
 for instance,
 where M became the largest party.

articles.title: Stora börsuppgångar, fortsätter de idag?
articles.heading: Morning Alert
articles.fulltext:
Internationellt
Jensen Huang tas tillbaka.
 I alla fall av Nvidias styrelse, efter påtryckningar från president Trump. Det förefaller enligt Bloomberg ha gått i rasande takt, utan att stämmas av med andra delar av företagsledningen än styrelsen. Huang är nu tillbaka efter 10 dagar, något som får nyhetsbyråer att damma av det gamla begreppet ”too-Big-to-Fail” men nu om en VD. Från regeringshåll sägs det ha varit utifrån aktieägarnas, anställdas, partners och kunders bästa intresse. Nyheten fick Nvidia-aktien att studsa upp 31%(!), efter att ha tappat 50% sedan 6 oktober, men den ligger fortfarande netto 31% ner från toppen.
Efter ett par turbulenta veckor fick händelsen att totalt ändra riktning på världens börser. S&P 500 steg med 4,7%, Nasdaq 6,5% och svenska OMXSPI 2,5%. Utvecklingen sprider sig genom handelssystemet och japanska Nikkei är nu på morgonen upp 4% och tekniktunga koreanska KOSPI ligger på +7%. Börsterminer pekar på svag uppgång idag. Tioåriga statsobligationsräntor har fallit något medan de tvååriga är i stort sett oförändrade eller upp någon enstaka räntepunkt. US-dollarn stärktes och ligger nu på 1,09, en nivå vi inte sett sedan de mest turbulenta dagarna kring ”Liberation Day”. Råoljepriset har nu också letat sig ner under 90 USD per fat, den lägsta nivån sedan slutet av augusti.
Dagens datakalender
 tar delvis vid efter gårdagens PMI med fler enkätundersökningar om tillförsikten framöver. I Tyskland kommer stora ifo-undersökningen och i USA konsumentförtroendet. Gårdagens PMI-undersökningar gav en blandad bild över Europa med fortsatt svagt läge i Frankrike som balanseras av att både industri och tjänstenäringar i Tyskland ser alltmer positivt på den närmaste framtiden.
Sverige
I 
Sweden 360
(varannan vecka) ligger det 
finansiella fokuset
 på förväntan om lägre utbud av nominella obligationer när Riksgälden släpper sin nya upplåningsrapport på torsdag. För kronan konstateras helt enkelt att börsfrossan den senaste tiden väger tungt på valutan. Vi drar också igång årets genomgång av kronans decemberutveckling. Historiskt har PPM -flödena försvagat kronan, men de senaste åren har det inte varit lika tydligt. I motsats har kronan snarare haft tendens att stärkas inför flödena.
Det 
politiska fokuset
 idag ligger på talmansrundorna (med start 09.30) inför en eventuell tredje statsministeromröstning. Utgången är lika svår att förutse som känslan är stark att samarbetsklimatet de senaste dagarna fått sig en törn på den rödgröna sidan. Nu meddelar också Centerpartiet att oklarheten gör att man gläntar på dörren till vad Kristersson har att erbjuda. Nu på morgonen presenterar SvD/Demoskop en ny opinionsundersökning (betallänk 
här
) där M når sin högsta nivå på över tio år. Det är i samma riktning som andra undersökningar den senaste tiden; opinionens dom av veckorna efter valet har primärt gynnat M. L ligger under 4%-spärren och både KD och SD har lägre procenttal än vid Riksdagsvalet. S tappar i denna undersökning stöd, men inte så mycket som i t ex senaste Novus där M blev största parti

articles.title: Risk-off move put SEK under pressure
articles.heading: Sweden 360
articles.fulltext:
Sweden 360 provides you with a quick and broad overview of Swedish macro, rates and FX.
*** See attachment for full report ***
Macro highlight: Riksbank – December rate hike unlikely
Riksbank hearing in Parliament:
 The overall tone was relatively balanced, suggesting further, gradual tightening. 
All Board members seem reluctant to provide firm guidance. Gov. Thedéen noted that rates “might need to rise once or a few more times, but it’s very uncertain”.
Economic activity was described as strong, although all members acknowledged the challenges facing households and businesses from higher energy prices and interest rates. The labour market assessment was nuanced.
Downplaying low inflation.
 The Board has seemed reluctant to attach much significance to low inflation, with none commenting directly on the large downside surprise in October.
December hike unlikely.
 Neither the hearing nor other communication since the November decision suggest that a rate hike in December is probable. 
Markets are pricing ~20% probability of a December hike and a full hike by March. While a Dec hike looks unlikely, we view pricing as broadly fair. However, market pricing indicate a high probability of two additional hikes, which we find too aggressive – look for opportunity to fade.
Rates highlights: 
NDO forecast – slightly lower nominal bond issuance in 2027
We predict that NDO will lower nominal bond issuance slightly in 2027
, compared to the plans from May, and reduce the number of weekly auctions to 45 from 48. This would bring total issuance to 225bn in 2027. 
Read more in our Preview:
SEB Research.
The central government budget balance has been SEK 40bn higher than the NDO’s May forecast. A one-off payment from the EU explains the stronger finances and both 
tax revenues and government expenditure have been broadly as expected
. 
According to the NDO’s May forecast, the budget balance will deteriorate significantly over the next 6 months. 
Stronger growth 
than the NDO projected implies that the underlying budget balance will be revised slightly higher. We expect the NDO’s 2026 GDP forecast will be revised 1pp higher. NDO will add 2028 to the forecast; the medium-term forecast will be important for issuance plans.
The outlook for fiscal policy is uncertain 
– budget rules imply tighter fiscal policy ahead, but messy government negotiations means that outlook is uncertain. 
Increased military spending and support for Ukraine will continue to exert downward pressure on the budget balance. Support to Ukraine has been delayed but seem to be largely in line with the NDO’s forecast.
The Riksbank will most likely request that the NDO borrows SEK200bn in foreign currency
 for re-lending as a hedge for the Riksbank’s currency reserve. The NDO will wait for a formal request before including this borrowing in the forecast but will probably 
discuss the implications in the report.
FX highlights I: Positioning reduction done – SEK sensitive to risk beta amid AI jitters  
‘Easy’ positioning correction over and done in EUR/SEK
. The potential for SEK short covering has played out and markets have turned their attention to the sell-off in equities, with risk-off weighing heavily on SEK. While positioning once again has turned clearly short SEK, CHF is likely to be the better trade among carry funders in general risk off environment.
FX highlights II: SEK with December seasonality but not in the beginning of the month
Less clear seasonal impact in the beginning of December. 
Historically, EUR/SEK tended to head higher early Dec in anticipation of the yearly premium pension dispersion – ”PPM-flows”. 
A large part of what is distributed was typically invested abroad and has therefore led to SEK outflows and a weaker SEK. T
he impact has faded in recent years as a large part of 
new payouts have been used to restore the fixed income allocation balance (mainly in SEK) in 
the default premium pension fund 
AP7 
Såfa
. 
However, since 2025, AP7 rebalances assets several times during the year, rather than once in Dec – potentially opening for a negative impact on the SEK if a larger share of payments are allocated in foreign equities. In any event, we do not expect any notable impact.
EUR/SEK still tends to fall in December as a whole. 
This is true versus EUR, USD as well as NOK:
EUR/SEK:
- Has fallen in Dec 12 out of the past 15 years by an average of -0.7%. 
- Has fallen 3 years in a row and by 1.3% in 2025.
USD/SEK:
- Has fallen in Dec 11 out of the past 15 years by an average of -1.2%.
- Fell by 2.5% in 2025.
NOK/SEK: 
- 
Has fallen in Dec 12 out of the past 15 years by an average of -0.8%.
 - 
Has fallen 2 years in a row and by 2.1% in 2025.
FX highlights III: 
NOK/SEK seasonality and resemblance to AUD/NZD turnaround
NOK/SEK turnaround. 
Seasonal patterns for NOK/SEK indicate a heightened probability for a turnaround to materialize already at the end of the year.
Should lower energy prices become more persistent, NOK would lose support from both its commodity beta and the carry-trade as market pricing on Norges Bank turns south, just as it already has done for AUD. 
The development in AUD/NZD – one carry investing currency with high-rate levels vs one carry funder with lower rate levels – where market pricing on RBA has fallen and taken AUD/NZD lower, works well as illustration of what ought to happen to NOK/SEK during 2027.
Upcoming data and events - what to watch?
Debt office report (Thu):
 We predict the NDO to lower 2027 nominal bond issuance by SEK 15bn to SEK 220bn, by reducing the number of weekly auctions to 45 from 48.
Final GDP (Fri):
 Household consumption and 
other expenditure side metrics imply that final Q3 GDP (presented November 27) will be revised higher compared to the flash estimate (0.4%, 2.8% y/y). Weak production in September is an uncertain factor, but there has been a downside bias for flash GDP vs final. We predict GDP to grow by 0.6%, 3.0% y/y (Riksbank 0.2%, 2.7% y/y). 
NIER survey (Fri): 
Business sentiment, most notably manufacturing, increased markedly in October, but consumer confidence (CCI) declined markedly indicating downside risks for household consumption during the 
autumn
 and winter. We predict CCI to decline further in November and predict business confidence will reverse parts of the strong increase in October.
Week Ahead: 
SEB Research

articles.title: NOK 2bn in NST481 and NST485
articles.heading: NGB Spotlight
articles.fulltext:
On Wednesday Nov 25th, Norges Bank will hold a multiple tap auction where a total of NOK 2bn will be issued, split between the NST481 (1.75%, 09/2029) and the NST485 (3.50%, 10/2042) bonds. NST481 currently trades with a yield of 4.525%, implying a maturity-matched spread vs. Germany of 144bps and an ASW spread of -21bps. NST485 trades with a yield of 4.12%, with corresponding spread levels at 54bps and -1bps. The auction closes at 11.00 CET, and results will be available on Norges Bank’s website at 11.05 CET. Ahead of the auction there will be a buyback auction of NST479 (1.75%, 02/2027) which closes at 10:00 CET.
On Wednesday, Norges Bank will auction a total of NOK 2bn split between NST481 (09/2029) and the NST485 (10/2042) bonds. These are the same bonds as in the previous auction which showed strong results and a high 9.7 bid-to-cover ratio in the shortest bond. Including the previous tap, NST485 has been included two times so far this year with an average bid-to-cover of 2.28 and allotment share of 35%. NST 481 has been included 7 times with an average bid-to-cover ratio of 4.83 and allotment share of 47%. Like the previous auction, we believe demand will be centered on NST481 and with the total volume capped at NOK 2bn we expect the auction to run smoothly. 
In addition, there will be a buyback auction of NST479 (02/2027). Outstanding amount before the auction (incl. government’s own holdings) is NOK 51.475bn. Short yields have rallied over the past week except for NST479 which has been trading sideways. This has led to a sharp inversion in the very front end of the yield curve. Hence, rolling into surrounding bonds from NST479 offers a negative yield pick-up. Norges Bank offered an ad-hoc buyback in conjunction with the previous auction (Nov 11) and a total of NOK 3.5bn was bought back. The auction closes at 10:00 CET, and announcement of the auction result will be released at 10:05 CET.
Market volatility has been high, with a sharp selloff in global equities last week providing support to bonds. Long Norwegian bonds have traded directional with global peers, and yields have fallen across the curve since the start of October, though most notably in the long end. Norwegian bonds have outperformed Germany in the rally, but underlying demand has been rather lackluster which is visible in the sharp underperformance against swaps. The risk-off sentiment triggered large receiving pressure in swaps throughout last week, especially in the front-end. The market now discounts only a 20% chance of another rate hike in total. Some probability of a rate cut is discounted from Sep 2027, while a full rate cut is priced from March 2028. We reiterate our forecast that the policy rate has likely peaked, and Norges Bank’s 
Q4 Inflation expectation survey
provided some support for our forecast. Our inflation forecast is higher than Norges Bank’s near-term trajectory, but we predict slightly lower core inflation in 2027.
Supply update: Following this auction, Norges Bank has issued a total of NOK 105bn YTD, while the annual borrowing interval is set at NOK 100-110bn (107-110bn in the Q4 guidance). We expect Norges Bank to issue the maximum amount, implying NOK 3bn in one of the 2 remaining auctions and NOK 2bn in the other. Looking ahead, the government’s budget proposal for 2027 showed an underlying borrowing requirement of NOK 93.6bn vs. 95.7bn in 2026. After years of under-borrowing, Norges Bank’s supply estimate has exceeded the underlying borrowing requirement over the past two years, with the aim of building up the cash reserves. We expect this to be the case also in 2027, implying a minimum of NOK 110bn in gross supply. The government’s borrowing mandate in long-term debt is increased by NOK 50bn to NOK 200bn, to provide greater flexibility and allowing for a potential increase in its own holdings. Risks to our supply estimate are thus skewed to the upside. Details will be provided in Norges Bank’s Strategy and borrowing programme due in December.

articles.title: Red warning sign – with a brave attempt at a rebound
articles.heading: Nordic Alert
articles.fulltext:
Global key stories
One big red warning sign – key takeaways.
 The Nasdaq plunged 
10%
 during an extremely volatile week for equities, with 5.3% of the decline coming on Friday alone. The S&P 500 and Sweden’s OMXSPI ended the week down 
8.6%
 and 
5.0%
, respectively. Many AI companies are trading at stretched valuations, but frankly, the potential of AI technology is extremely difficult – if not impossible – to quantify. From an economist’s perspective, there are 
three reasons
 behind the AI sell-off: 
(1)
 signs of increasing 
political intervention in AI
, reflecting 
shifting power dynamics in Washington
 and Trump’s decision to 
penalise US companies seeking to build data centres abroad
; 
(2)
rising short- and long-term real interest rates
, forcing a more aggressive discounting of future earnings – i.e. lower equity valuations – while also raising funding costs; and 
(3) seasonal factors
, as major investors seek to 
“close their books”
 and lock in strong performance figures ahead of year-end. This increases the risk of deteriorating market liquidity, potentially amplifying price swings. Analysts – and economists – now need to distinguish between AI valuations and the long-term impact of these transformative technologies on growth, inflation and productivity. Anthropic shares, which surged 17% on their market debut on Thursday, also lost ground but remain 7% above their IPO price. The US 10-year Treasury yield fell by as much as 11 basis points on Friday to 4.95%, while movements in the dollar and oil (Brent) were relatively modest. Thursday’s Thanksgiving holiday will reduce market liquidity. Early on Monday, equity markets are attempting to rebound, with Nasdaq futures currently up 2.3% (see table below for other market quotes). 
A complicated world for central banks – reflections.
 In just over two weeks, the Fed will announce its next rate decision. At the time of writing, markets are pricing in a 94% probability of a 25-basis-point hike to 4.25%. It remains to be seen how the Fed – and other central banks – will navigate the new risk environment: high inflation and still-solid GDP prospects, now set against less supportive financial conditions (see chart below) and falling equity markets. The question is whether an equity market correction, within reasonable limits, might even be welcomed by the ECB and the Bank of Japan, both of which are also expected to raise their policy rates in December.
An extraordinary trilateral meeting with little substance – epilogue.
 Last week’s Xi-Putin-Trump meeting was a Russian PR success, but hardly a Yalta 2.0 – despite the Kremlin’s efforts. Trump continues, rather astonishingly, to 
refer to Putin as “my friend”. President Zelenskyy says: “To us, he is a murderer.”
 A sign of the times, reflecting the erosion of the rules-based international order and its replacement by an increasingly power-based one: 
on Friday, the UN Security Council failed – for the ninth consecutive time – to
 appoint a new UN Secretary-General. A weakened and increasingly marginalised António Guterres will leave the UN in six weeks. 
Conclusion:
 Geopolitical unpredictability must become a permanent parameter in economic forecasts. 
The next major geopolitical event:
the G20 summit in Florida on 14–15 December
, offering Trump an excellent photo opportunity on home turf. Putin has been invited, but his attendance remains unconfirmed. Notably, Europe will have a substantial presence this time – compared with Shenzhen.
Pro-EU Burnham faces a delicate political balancing act over “Breturn” – key takeaways.
Friday’s new agreement
 confirms that the gap between London and Brussels continues to narrow. However, just over 60% of Britons still oppose rejoining the EU. The new agreement sets out a timetable for food exports and emissions trading, as well as for implementing proposals to facilitate greater mobility for young people. Prime Minister Burnham, who has already made clear his ambition to forge even closer ties with the EU, claims that the new agreement will “boost UK GDP by up to 0.5%”. Does the EU want Britain back? Political fragmentation within the EU, against the backdrop of an emerging new world order, is increasing the bloc’s interest in bringing a major global player back into the fold as that new order takes shape. This means that the UK should by no means be regarded as the weaker party in the ongoing talks between Brussels and London.
Nordic key stories
70 days without a Swedish government – some reflections.
 “No, but no thanks” was the Left Party’s swift and clear response to the weekend’s offer from the three red-green parties. Government negotiations (S+C+MP+V) are progressing at a snail’s pace – like a snail crawling uphill on a sand-covered slope with the handbrake on. Frustration is growing among voters. A new TV4/Novus poll shows that 44% favour a snap election, while 36% oppose it. The question now is: will the Centre Party switch sides and join the right-wing “Alliance”? Keep an eye on 27 November, the deadline for parties to submit their alternative budget proposals. This could provide an opportunity to abandon – or at least amend – the caretaker budget if an alternative proposal secures support in parliament.
